test_title: RRB NTPC - UG 2025 (CBT 1) Mid-Range Full Test - 04
subject: general
question:
Arrange the following from South to North sequence.

I. Pirpanjal range

II. Zanskar range

III. Greater Himalayas

IV. Ladakh range

Select the correct answer from the code given below:

Code:
solution:
**The correct answer is: I, III, II, IV**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Pir Panjal Range (I):

 
 
• Located to the south of the main Himalayas, it is part of the Lesser Himalayas.
 
• Forms the southernmost major range in the sequence.
 
• Acts as a barrier between the Kashmir Valley and the outer plains.
 
 
 
• Greater Himalayas / Himadri (III):
 
 
• Situated to the north of the Pir Panjal range.
 
• Contains the world’s highest peaks including Mount Everest and Kanchenjunga.
 
• Characterized by perennial snow cover and glaciers.
 
 
 
• Zanskar Range (II):
 
 
• Lies to the north of the Greater Himalayas.
 
• Separates the Zanskar Valley from Ladakh.
 
• Known for deep gorges and rugged terrain.
 
 
 
• Ladakh Range (IV):
 
 
• The northernmost among the given ranges.
 
• Part of the Trans-Himalayan region extending into Tibet.
 
• Characterized by barren landscapes and high-altitude cold deserts.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The Himalayas are broadly divided into three parallel ranges from south to north: the Shiwaliks (Outer Himalayas), the Lesser Himalayas (including Pir Panjal), and the Greater Himalayas (Himadri).
 
• Beyond the Greater Himalayas lie the Trans-Himalayan ranges, which include Zanskar, Ladakh, and Karakoram ranges.
 
• The Ladakh and Zanskar ranges form important watersheds, influencing the flow of rivers like the Indus and its tributaries.
 
• These ranges are not only geographically significant but also strategically important due to their proximity to international borders.
